name: A Kent County farm lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Kent County, Delaware (Q128137), coordinate location (P625)

blurb: A farm lot on the flat coastal plain of Kent County, Delaware: a weathered barn and outbuildings, a mown yard and a vegetable patch, a hedgerow and a block of oak, hickory and loblolly pine along the field edge. Cardinals, blue jays, crows and doves work the yard by day, cottontails slip out at dusk, and raccoons and foxes visit after dark.

facts.text: Kent County has a humid subtropical climate (Koppen Cfa); all months average above freezing and the USDA hardiness zone is 7b.

source.title: Wikipedia: Kent County, Delaware

facts.text: Kent County's county seat is Dover, the capital of Delaware; the county is named for the English county of Kent.

source.title: Wikipedia: Kent County, Delaware
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Kent County, Delaware", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: About 26.6% of Kent County's area is water, and through the late 18th century its economy was based on small grain farms.

source.title: Wikipedia: Kent County, Delaware
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Kent County, Delaware", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The American robin, listed for this locale, is the most abundant landbird in North America, with an estimated 370 million individuals.

source.title: Wikipedia: American robin

facts.text: The public centroid of Kent County, Delaware (39.10 N, 75.50 W) lies about 5 m above sea level.
